newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner's Lipp-states must win EMU entry on merit.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner's Lipp-states must win EMU entry on merit.

text.p: Ernst-Moritz Lipp, board member at Germany's Dresdner Bank AG, said on Friday that decisions on which countries should take part in monetary union should not be made on a poltical basis.

Calling for a strict application of the entry criteria as the basis to decide which countries will enter monetary union inn 1999, Lipp said "We do not want a political decision seeking the largest possible or smallest possible group."

He added that any comments of this type immediately threw the political question of which nations qualified to the fore, which then also put a spotlight on questions such as whether one EU member could enter EMU without another.
Lipp added that Spain currently looked like a potential candidate to qualify for EMU entry and denied that Dresdner believed Spain should not be in the first group.

At the World Economic Forum in Davos this month, Lipp had commented that it could be difficult to persuade Italy to delay its entry to European Monetary Union if Spain was allowed in at the euro's launch in 1999.

Countries which want to meld their currencies in the euro in 1999 have to meet certain economic targets this year. But the final decision on who qualifies will be taken by political leaders in March 1998.
